full_judgment:
6. Mr. S.K. Sinha, the learned Advocate appearing for accused appellants Lal Miah and Gourango Chandra Nath submits that the trial held by the Additional Sessions Judge is vitiated by Misjoinder of Charges and persons. He submits that the alleged offences under sections 395/397/325/34 and 302/34 of the Penal Code being not committed in course of the same transaction the case of the appellants did neither fall within the purview of sec. 235 nor within that of Sec. 239 Cr. P.C. By joining the charges together in a single trial, the learned Judge has committed an illegality which has vitiated the trial. 

 16. Adoption of a procedure which is positively prohibited by the Cr.P.C. Where the defect has occasioned an injustice in the sense that the accused were embarrassed in their defence in having to meet a multifarious accumulation of evidence upon a diversity of Counts, several of which were illegally joined in the trial, such defect cannot be cured by section 537 Cr.P.C. and the trial is illegal. It is held in the decision reported in 10 D.L.R. (S.C) 29 that joint trial held on the offences charged not committed within the same transaction is illegal and not curable under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Whether joint trial is illegal or irregular, the test is whether accused has been prejudiced by such trial or not, and whether there occasioned any failure of justice by holding such trial. If prejudice is caused by occasioning failure of justice, such trial is positively illegal. In the instant case we have seen that the occurrence took place on 1.3.75 and the trial started on 18.8.84, and concluded on 9th December, 1984 taking a long period of about 9 years and the accused appellants had to face a number of charges in place of one and they appeared to have been bewildered and embarrassed in having to defend themselves against such numerous charges. This illegal joinder of charges which did not form part of the same transaction, in the facts and circumstances of the case, leads to a clear presumption of prejudice caused to the accused appellants occasioning failure of justice. So we find from the aforesaid decisions that the trial of the accused appellants and others having been concluded by misjoinder of charges prohibited by law which in our opinion is illegal and the trial is vitiated thereby. 

 17. A view expressed in A.I.R. 1947 and 35 D.L.R. P. 243 that as a result of joinder of charges illegally, the case should be sent for retrial. Billina case where a joinder of charges is not only illegal but also prejudicial to the accused appellants occasioning a failure of justice, the only order needs be passed is an order of acquittal in favour of the accused. In the decision of Nasiruddin Vs. Appellate Tribunal reported in 31 D.L.R. (AD) 312 it has been held, "in the face of the record, which according to the learned Judge vitiated the trial occasioning failure of justice only appropriate order that ought to have been passed was an order declaring the order of conviction and sentence to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect in the instant case also when we are of the view that an illegal trial as held by the learned Additional Sessions Judge by misjoinder of charges and accused persons, has vitiated the entire trial occasioning a failure of justice. We are reluctant to send the case for retrial and we hold that the accused appellants are entitled to an order of acquittal in such circumstances. From the judgment it appears that as many as 4 accused were convicted, of them Lal Miah and Gourango Chandra Nath have preferred this appeal and other two accused Abdul Halim and Mayecnuddin are absconding till today. The entire order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge is hereby set aside.
